label: Intrinsic to a bearer from w: actual-relative supervenience on its real determinations
definition: IntrinsicTo o Has w g e := ∀ v, o.frame.access w v → (∀ d, Has v g d ↔ Has w g d) → (e v ↔ e w). A world-predicate e is intrinsic to the bearer g from w when, at every world accessible from w at which g has exactly the real determinations (Has) it has at w, e has the same truth value as at w. It is an actual-relative supervenience criterion: it compares each accessible world only with w, not arbitrary pairs of worlds, and only over worlds where g's whole profile of determinations matches its actual one. It is not membership in Has: e need not be a determination, or mention g at all. It admits every predicate that is constant over the accessible worlds, including necessarily true extrinsic predicates (for example 'something exists'), and any predicate that happens to covary with g's profile over the accessible worlds. So 'no intrinsic fact discriminates' in the certificates means: no predicate meeting this criterion discriminates; it is not a claim about a narrower metaphysical notion of intrinsicness. It carries over to an intrinsic property in a narrower sense only if that property supervenes on g's Has-profile at the accessible worlds, an open bridge (that Has exhausts g's intrinsic nature) not asserted here.
note: Stipulated for #2145 lane M (relation-of-reason certificate 8347844a, clause 1; mirror fork 59278450, clause 6), after the Codex review of #2179 (comment 4723571352). Settled by Lean: the definition is the body of IntrinsicTo. Its scope matters because the certificates' contrast result is proved for exactly this class: when g's profile is invariant over the accessible worlds (IntrinsicProfileInvariant), every IntrinsicTo predicate is constant over them and so cannot discriminate anything that fails at some accessible world. Examples: g's having a determination d (Has · g d) is IntrinsicTo g; a constant predicate is. Non-examples: the terminus of g's act in the relation-of-reason carrier (it differs between accessible worlds where g's profile is the same); 'the effect exists' there. Distinguished from the real determinations themselves (Has), from Lewis-style intrinsicness (duplication-invariance across all worlds) and from N (906f9077), which constrains Has, not predicates.
